summary:
# NOTES: Two-book corpus (for detailed Q&A)

## BOOK 1: ADVENTURES OF BINDLE (Herbert Jenkins)

**Front matter:** "What this book is about": Bindle, furniture remover; sequel to *The Night Club*. Dedicated "To the Children of the Dead End". Twelfth printing, 167,461 copies. Chapter list: I Coming of the Lodger; II Downing Street Sensation; III Air-Raid; IV Duplication of Mr. Hearty; V Gathering of the Bands; VI Mr. Gupperduck's Mishap; VII Courting of Rev. Andrew MacFie; VIII Chapel Conversazione; IX Letting of Number Six; X Downfall of Mr. Jabez Stiffson; XI Camouflaging of Mr. Gupperduck; XII Tragedy of Giuseppi Antonio Tolmenicino; XIII Return of Charlie Dixon; XIV Mr. Hearty Yields; XV A Billeting Adventure; XVI Millie's Wedding.

**Core cast:** Joseph "Bindle" (J.B.; special constable, Fulham; cricket cap blue/white triangles; pipe; "little jokes"; wife's nickname "Mrs. B."). Mrs. Lizzie Bindle (sister of Martha; religious, chapel, Alton Road Chapel; bangs dishes; asks "Got a job?"; married 19 years). Alfred "Mr. Hearty" (greengrocer, shops in Fulham, Putney, Wandsworth; woolly voice; "Earty"). Martha Hearty (wheezes, "my breath"). Millie Hearty (Millikins, niece, ~18). Charlie Dixon (Sergeant, 110th Service Battalion London Regt; Millie's sweetheart). Josiah Gupperduck (lodger; accordion; "sower of the seed"; Society for Suppression of Atheism). Ginger (gloomy mate, "I don't 'old wiv" ...), Wilkes (coughs constantly), Huggles (grins; drives), Ruddy Bill, Tippitt, Smith (Hearty's assistant), Billy Nips (errand boy). Guggers (Captain, Gordons; "gug-gug"; 14 stone; Spit-and-Speak). Dick Little and Tom Little (doctor's sons, Chelsea flat). Lady Knob-Kerrick (Barton Bridge, The Poplars Putney Hill; lorgnettes), Miss Strint (companion), John (footman, "Calves"), Mr. Wilton (butler), Mrs. Marlings (housekeeper). Rev. Andrew MacFie (Scottish, Alton Road Chapel; "Meester Beendle"); Miss MacFie (sister). Rev. James Sopley (retiring pastor; ceiling-gazing).

### Ch I The Coming of the Lodger
- Supper row. Mrs. Bindle shows ad in *The Gospel Sentinel*: "CHRISTIAN HOME wanted by a single gentleman, chapel-goer, temperance, quiet, musical, home-comforts, good-cooking, moderate terms... Apply Lonely, c/o The Gospel Sentinel."
- Bindle's Horace Gaze story (returned soldier catches wife at back door). "Lodgers ain't to be trusted."
- Mrs. Bindle forbids smoking; Bindle: "'Oly Angels!"; "Remember" (her word).
- Lodger Mr. Josiah Gupperduck arrives Monday 8 p.m.: small, thin, round spectacles, three wisps of hair, short brown beard, red nose, ears like sign-boards. Bindle's "pleasant for the ducks... not for Gupperducks." Lodger's sermon style ("peace that passeth all understanding"); invents Scripture.
- Bindle's "Gospel Bells" (Mrs. B's hymn); "If You Squeeze Me Tighter, Jimmie, I Shall Scream."
- Bindle's "lodger" essay (nations rose and fell; lodger stayed on).
- Bindle's "stealing" remark. Bindle: "Mrs. B. ... Gupperduck" joke; "Mrs. B., you're fickle."

### Ch II A Downing Street Sensation
- Bindle hired by Messrs. Empsom & Daley (cartage; foreman). Rides horse with Tippitt (weedy, cigarette on lip; "On 'is tail"). Spotty (stable-hand) leg-ups. Bindle falls, walks, boards bus to Wimbledon Common; Drag and Hounds, Green Lion pubs.
- Delivery: pantechnicon of John Smith & Co., Merton; two ladies (elder sallow, pince-nez; younger driver). Destination: Mr. Llewellyn John, 110 Downing Street. Van claims "carved-oak dining-room furniture". Lady gives 2s.
- Bindle buys lamp-black at oil-shop (Wimbledon High St; young woman); waters van roof with watering-can (borrowed from barman at Green Lion), tarpaulin; puffs lamp-black through roof air-holes with pea-puffer.
- Key handed by lady opposite Houses of Parliament; Bindle engages inspector: "Black and White Raiders" (suffragettes).
- Van opened in Downing Street: ~20 women blackened with lamp-black; Tippitt knocked down; police whistle. Women shepherded to Whitehall; taxis refuse; "Go 'ome and wash the baby." Women go to Tube/District Railway to Wimbledon.
- Chief-Inspector Gunny (Scotland Yard) praises Bindle; Deputy-Commissioner gives cigar. Bindle: "Joseph Bindle's my name. I'm a special, Fulham district." Ends at The Feathers.

### Ch III The Air-Raid
- I: Bindle, special constable, at Hearty's. Gupperduck and Hearty fearful; Mrs. Hearty; Millie loyal. Bindle: "The Barker" (gun). Hearty, Gupperduck, Mrs. Bindle hide in potato cellar.
- II: Bindle drops scales (7 lb weights) on trap-door (prank). Gupperduck loses spectacles and upper false teeth. Mrs. Bindle faints (carried by Hearty & Gupperduck). "All Clear" (two long notes). Millie: "Nobody didn't ought to mind sayin' they're afraid."

### Ch IV The Duplication of Mr. Hearty
- I: Mrs. Bindle: "You've never been a real husband." Bindle: "Gawd made me, an' Gawd made 'Earty... made a bloomer." Stewed-steak-and-onions; apple-pudding. Bindle visits Dick Little (Chelsea flat); Tom Little; Guggers (Spit-and-Speak; Oxford rag; "gug-gug"). Plan: publicity stunt against Hearty's third shop (Putney High St).
- II: Hearty's Putney shop (green paint, brass). Six duplicates of Hearty, each greeting "Good afternoon, Joseph," each asking for a cauliflower. Smith sees them through cellar flap. Mrs. Hearty laughs. Hearty: "Joseph, I give these men in charge." Duplicates march out playing tin whistles (hymns; "Men of Harlech").

### Ch V The Gathering of the Bands
- Donkeys with boards: "ALFRED HEARTY THE NAPOLEON OF GREENGROCERS", "THE CAESAR OF FRUITERERS", "PINEAPPLE ALF", "HEARTY'S TWO-SHILLING PINEAPPLE TRY IT IN YOUR BATH", "GENERAL ALLENBY EATS THEM", "IF YOU DON'T BUY YOUR VEGETABLES FROM ALFRED HEARTY YOU WILL BE WHAT I AM", "THEY CURE BALDNESS".
- Camel: "I'VE GOT THE HUMP THROUGH NOT BUYING HEARTY'S VEGETABLES"; "EAT HEARTY'S LEEKS THEY DEFY THE PLUMBER".
- Bands: "Pull for the Shore, Sailor"; "Onward Christian Soldiers" (leader upstairs, tall weary cornet, "Charlie"); "Shall We Gather at the River"; "Gospel Bells"; "The Last Noel" (eighth band). Drummers stuck in doorway (Ted; Striker). Short genial green-and-yellow band leader with Razor. Inspector, obstruction, summons threat. Mrs. Bindle: "That Bindle's done this."

### Ch VI Mr. Gupperduck's Mishap
- Gupperduck late; Mrs. Bindle worried. Bindle: Hearty summoned to police court over bands.
- Two supporters (weedy man with sandy pointed beard, cloth cap; little man with long beard) bring battered Gupperduck from Hyde Park Peace meeting (wounded soldiers; resolution against war). Man climbed tree ("Peter"). Gupperduck's face: black eye, broken lip, bloody ear; lost hat, spectacles, collar. Bindle gives him half-quartern whisky; Mrs. Bindle: "He's temperance." Mrs. Bindle nurses him; Gupperduck: "The Lord hath given me rest from mine enemies."
- Bindle: "it's still more wonderful wot a crowd can do with a man." "Because you haven't got a soul." / "flea-powder... soul-powder."

### Ch VII The Courting of the Rev. Andrew MacFie
- Millie left home over Hearty's remark about Charlie; refused return until apology. Charlie to front (Sergeant).
- Lady Knob-Kerrick brings MacFie (Barton Bridge) to Alton Road Chapel after Sopley retires. Temperance Fete fiasco: lemonade with crude alcohol and distilled mead (Bindle did it); MacFie drunk, assaulted police; "lemon-and-a-mac" drink named after him at The Two-Faced Earl, The Blue Fox.
- MacFie visits Mrs. Bindle's kitchen; asks about Millie's absence from chapel; Bindle catches them ("'Ullo, caught you"). Bindle: "I'd rather Kiss the Mistress than the Maid."
- Bindle to Hearty: "that sandy-'aired son of a tub-thumper." Hearty: "Joseph... you must cease to interfere."
- Uriah the Hittite story told at Hearty's Sunday supper; Millie: "If I had been her, I should have killed David." Hearty: "Millie, we will have a hymn." Bindle: "Sprague's Fulham Whiffs" (smoke). "Lord Windover" referenced. Millie: "I understood."

### Ch VIII The Chapel Conversazione
- Conversazione in Chapel school-room; Hearty's furniture; texts ("Prepare to Meet Thy God", "The Wages of Sin is Death", "And So Shall Ye All Likewise Perish"). Refreshments: fish-paste sandwiches, three-cornered tarts.
- Miss MacFie (tall, flat-chested). Alice (maid announces names wrongly: "Mr. Muddenham and Mr. Tuskett"; "Mr. Pip-Pip"; "Miss Musk-Rat"). Guests: Mr. Pain & "wife" (Mrs. Pain); Mr. and Mrs. Withers; Mr. Tuddenham (red, fierce) & Mr. Muskett (white beard, pince-nez); Miss Torkington (princess-robe; Bindle's text joke offends her); Mr. and Mrs. Gash (butcher); Mr. Hippitt; Mrs. Muspratt; Mr. Sopley.
- Glee party: "The Glad Eye" song; Mrs. Bindle stops falsetto.
- Lady K's speech: Sopley presented illuminated address, £50 purse, silver-mounted hot-water bottle. Bindle interjects "Temperance fetes!"
- Woman "Mrs. Helen"/claimed wife: "My Andrew!" — actually Pierrette "Nancy" Dane (Private, Passchendaele Pierrots) in disguise, arranged by Dick Little & Bindle, to humiliate MacFie (wife claim "secret marriage"). MacFie: "It's a lee!" John blows police-whistle; false raid alarm; trains stopped, ambulances summoned.
- Bindle to Dick Little's flat: "Pore ole Mac... got the wind up." Summonses dismissed (Lady K, John); magistrate's remark. MacFie's £20 advertisement offer.

### Ch IX The Letting of Number Six
- I: Mrs. Bindle: "An' what am I to do if there's an air-raid?" Bindle takes temporary porter job at Fulham Square Mansions (replacing Charlie Hart on holiday; Mrs. Hart ill). Mrs. Sedge (Mrs. Hart's mother; "Royal Richard" = gin; "Kilburn Cemetery" = pub). Number Seven (ex-Indian civil servant, choleric). Queenie (maid of Number Eight). Number Twelve (lost Fluffles, Pekinese). Number Eleven (old lady; postage stamp). Number One (parcel). Bindle wears special's uniform on leisure.
- II: Number Six (two bedrooms, sitting-room, bathroom, kitchen) let to Mr. Jabez Stiffson (3½ guineas/week; canary Oscar; bald, black whiskers, side-whiskers?, spectacles) — wife Mrs. Stiffson staying with friends; arrives Tuesday. Miss Cissie Boye (actress, revue "Kiss Me Quick" at Regent Theatre; honey-coloured fluffy hair; "a call" 11 a.m.) arrives near midnight by taxi. Miss Boye's "Bobbie" mentioned.

### Ch X The Downfall of Mr. Jabez Stiffson
- I: Morning: Mrs. Sedge (Royal Richard). Cissie Boye in dressing-gown: "there's a man in my bath." Stiffson in pink bath-robe and yellow felt slippers. Bindle: "What the wife don't see the 'usband don't 'ave to explain." Stiffson dressed in tweed trousers, spats; breakfast with Cissie. Bindle sets clock back. Oscar fed.
- II: Mrs. Stiffson (tall, grey hair) arrives; Bindle stalls; she climbs stairs. Tableau: coffee cup spilled on waistcoat. "Jabez!" "I thought I told you to wear your tweed mixture to-day." Mrs. Sedge brings porridge; Mrs. Stiffson smashes porridge bowl on Stiffson's head. Hysterics; Mrs. Stiffson flees into lift; lift stuck halfway; Number Seven: "Damned old tiger-cat!" Mr. Stiffson, luggage, thermos and Oscar flee. Bindle warns Mrs. Stiffson.

### Ch XI The Camouflaging of Mr. Gupperduck
- I: Yellow Ostrich bar; Ginger (gloomy; no hand-shake), Wilkes (coughs), Huggles (grins). Ruddy Bill's rift with landlord at The Scarlet Horse (Bill: "a ruddy donkey behind the bar"). Bindle tells Gupperduck's Putney Heath/Hyde Park humiliation. Ginger: "Why don't they make peace?" Bindle: "no dinner-hour" Lloyd George/ King George V jokes; "billy-goats."
- II: Mrs. Bindle asks "Where's Mr. Gupperduck?" Hearty and Bindle discuss. Gupperduck attacked after "Peace" meeting in Hyde Park (Mr. Llewellyn John mentioned). Peter (sandy beard) betrayed; Mr. Wayskin (little bespectacled man with long beard, fled). Bindle: "If ever I catches Mr. Josiah Gupperduck... I'll camelflage 'im."

### Ch XII The Tragedy of Giuseppi Antonio Tolmenicino
- I: Scratcher (lantern-jawed, fishy eyes) now waiter at Napolini's, Regent Street. Bindle hired; Scratcher: "Four pound last week." Ginger's free drink.
- II: Bindle's assistant "Giuseppi Antonio Tolmenicino" (fierce moustache). Bindle nicknames him "Kayser"; Tolmenicino hates it. Bindle's "bouillabaisse", "caille en casserole" confusion, curried prawns, Welsh rarebit on lady's chest. Champagne cork wrecks dining room; Bindle puts bottle in hot water. Tolmenicino attacks Bindle with bottle, hits another waiter; collides with Herr Smith (James Smith, formerly Herr Siegesmann, chief superintendent, Dundreary whiskers; "Berlice!"). Tolmenicino arrested; documents found under Defence of the Realm Act (spy). Bindle to Marlborough Street Police Court next day. Bindle leaves Napolini's: "So the Lodger Pawned His Second Pair of Boots."

### Ch XIII The Return of Charlie Dixon
- Millie thrilled; Charlie home 10 days' leave. Bindle, Millie, Charlie at Universal Cafe (dinner 3s 6d; band; "Number 68" wine = champagne). Charlie proposes marriage before he returns to France. Bindle: "Marry Charlie Dixon, and do the ole Kayser in." Bindle to confront Hearty. Millie: "Father wouldn't let me." Bindle: "I'll eat my 'at."
- Bindle to Charlie: "Your friendship 'urts like 'ell."

### Ch XIV Mr. Hearty Yields
- Mrs. Bindle: "Look at Mr. Hearty." Bindle: "Gawd started makin' a man..." Bindle to Heartys' house; Mr. Hearty refuses; Bindle threatens; Mr. Hearty fears revelation (secret; "Six-an'-Eightpence" lawyer; "a clue"; "Mrs. ... the Ole Bird on the 'Ill" — Bindle's bluff about a woman who'd tell Lady K). Hearty consents: "Joseph... Millie." Bindle: "Pore little Millikins!" Mr. Hearty stiff. Wedding set for Tuesday.

### Ch XV A Billeting Adventure
- Ginger on leave helps; Bindle, Ginger, Wilkes, Huggles on Harridge's Stores pantechnicon. Putney Hill, The Poplars (Lady K). Bindle reads delivery-note: "Sixteen bedsteads, bedding, four baths, four washin' stands" for "Fit up bedsteads in drawin'-room for billetin' soldiers." Mr. Wilton and John (footman). Mrs. Marlings. Bindle places wallet/ Huggles hat on bust of late Sir Benjamin Biggs. Ginger's red herring fried; Ginger "I don't 'old wiv ruddy waiters." Lady K: "Why are you not in the army?" Bindle: "You got 'various' veins in your legs, mum?" Ginger: "I seen 'im!" Sixteen soldiers (sergeant) arrive; Lady K sends them away; Bindle's joke. Lady K's threats; Harridge's account closed. "Are we downhearted? Noooo!"

### Ch XVI Millie's Wedding
- Bindle with crush hat, canary gloves, white rose; Mrs. Bindle green bonnet, maroon dress. Mr. Hearty's hat under carriage; dog's paw. Millie wears grey coat and skirt. Rev. Sopley officiates (from Eastbourne), gloomy. Mr. Dixon (Charlie's uncle, John Dixon, "beer!"); Mrs. Dixon (gentle, white hair). Bindle's "Lost the cup" joke; "Gentlemen twins" joke; Mr. Sopley's sermon. Bindle's speech: "marriages is made in Fulham," "bottles is returnable." Mrs. Dixon: "You must be a very good man." Bindle and Mr. Dixon walk toward Putney Bridge.
- END OF BOOK 1.

## BOOK 2: BINDLE: SOME CHAPTERS IN THE LIFE OF JOSEPH BINDLE (Herbert Jenkins, 1916)

**Front matter:** Quote from T. P. O'Connor, M.P.: "Bindle is the greatest Cockney that has come into being through the medium of literature since Dickens wrote Pickwick Papers." Dedicated "To My Mother." Foreword by H. J. (author-publisher): Blackwood's account; suggestion by William Blackwood. Address: 12 Arundel Place, Haymarket. Dated August 1916. Contents: I The Bindles at Home; II A Nocturnal Adventure; III The Hypnotic Fiasco; IV The Heartys at Home; V Bindle Tries a Change of Work; VI The Hotel Corridor; VII Bindle Commits an Indiscretion; VIII The Great Conspiracy; IX The Temperance Fete; X Mr. Hearty Prays for Bindle; XI Mr. Hearty Becomes Extremely Unpopular; XII Bindle Agrees to Become a Millionaire; XIII Oxford's Welcome to Bindle; XIV Mr. Hearty Gives a Party; XV Bindle and the German Menace; XVI The Amateur Detectives; XVII Bindle Makes a Mistake; XVIII Bindle Assists in an Elopement; XIX The Scarlet Horse Coterie; XX Millie Leaves Home; XXI Conclusion.

**Additional cast:** Professor Sylvanus Conti (real name Willie Wilkins; hypnotist; 13 Audrey Mansions, Queen's Club, West Kensington; rival "Mr. John Gibson, the English Mesmerist"). Mr. Gandy (landlord, Dove and Easel, Little Compton, Suffolk). Mrs. Gandy. Sir Charles Custance J.P. (The Towers). Mr. Roger Greenhales (Home Farm). Sergeant Wrannock (Suffolk Constabulary). Mrs. Grinder (shop). Brooks (foreman). Mr. Henry (Richard) Miller (gun collection, Holmleigh). Sanders (foreman, Splendid Hotel). Mr. and Mrs. Railton-Rogers (Emily, Albert?; children Eustace, Nelly, Muriel; nurse). Mrs. Clark (neighbour) and son Archie Clark; Ruthie (maid). Mr. and Mrs. Daniel Granger (33 Lebanon Avenue, Chiswick). Dick Little's fiancée Ethel Knob-Kerrick. Reginald Graves (St. Joseph's College, Oxford; scholarship; "Gravy"); Dr. Peter (Master); Dick Travers; Horace Trent (cox, kangaroo costume); Edward Winch (missionary, Ch XIV); Mr. Sopley; Mr. Flinders (grocer); Cave; Ruddy Bill; Weary; Whiskers; Ted; Ginger; Wilkes; Huggles; Tom Cave.

### Ch I The Bindles at Home
- Blue Boar pub, Hammersmith. Bindle and Ginger: "Women is all right if yer can keep 'em from marryin' yer." Ginger's gloom; three babies. Bindle's father "drunk 'isself to death 'keepin' the chill out"; "'Gospel Bells.'" Bindle's "tack" and "tin o' salmon" tactic. "I'd kill a slop."
- Bindle's job history; furniture-removal "bespattered quarter-days." Mrs. Bindle's religion ("Dirt and the Devil"); bath episode (Bindle rubs hands on boots). Mrs. Bindle mocks: "Why don't you stick at somethin'?" Mr. Hearty as model.
- Home: Mrs. Bindle asks "Got a job?"; Bindle lies "night watchman at a garridge" (9 p.m.). Stewed steak and onions. Parlour (antimacassars, musical box). Clock stopped; Bindle pawns clock (7 shillings). Mrs. Bindle: "I'd steal 'fore I'd do that." Bindle contemplates theft.

### Ch II A Nocturnal Adventure
- Bindle finds keys (Professor Sylvanus Conti, 13 Audrey Mansions, Queen's Club, West Kensington; reward 2s 6d). Has duplicates cut at stall (1s). Bindle at Purple Goat; buys electric torch; bandages head and face (medical bandaging). Enters No. 13 with duplicate keys; rings bell; returns keys to porter (reward).
- Porter tells tale of bus/fire-engine collision (11 deaths).
- Conti's rival John Gibson; Conti's watch (gold hunter, "A few friends and admirers"), money on bedside table. Conti wakes: burglar's torch. Conti with revolver; Bindle hands up. Handcuffs. Bindle: "This comes o' takin' advice of a 'daughter o' the Lord.'" Conti hypnotises Bindle (card: "PROFESSOR SYLVANUS CONTI, Hypnotist and Mesmerist"). Bindle repeats: "I am a burglar." Conti writes note to police; Bindle must deliver it. Bindle shows goods (watch, chain, scarf-pin, sleeve-links, studs, diamond ring); Conti dismisses him.

### Ch III The Hypnotic Fiasco
- Bindle walks, whistles; laughs at police; coffee-stall. Gives note to a labourer (with a shilling) "burglary and murder," runs off.
- Conti telephones police; bragging to newspaper *The Evening Mail*; placard "MESMERISM EXTRAORDINARY / AN AMAZING CAPTURE / ALLEGED BURGLAR HYPNOTISED".
- West London Police Court: Bindle (arrested) protests "Me a burglar?" Conti sworn; says prisoner isn't the man. Conti's humiliation. Newspaper: "PROFESSOR CONTI'S GREAT HYPNOTIC FEAT". Bindle returns swag by post (small change, two duplicate keys).
- Evening Post account: magistrate: "Professor Conti sought advertisement; he has got it." Bindle winks.

### Ch IV The Heartys at Home
- Mr. Hearty: spare, heavy moustache, iron-grey mutton-chop whiskers, woolly voice; sucks moustache; fears Bindle. Mrs. Hearty fat, laughs silently; Bindle tells stories. Millie.
- Mrs. Bindle regrets marrying Bindle (chose Bindle over Hearty; Hearty "got on"). Bindle: "If 'e 'ad 'ad a little more ginger..."
- Sunday evening hymns; Bindle sings "Pull for the Shore, Sailors" and "Gospel Bells" loudly. Mrs. Hearty collapses. Bindle's missionary anecdote (double-bed, grandfather clock with weights in tea-things, jungle). Bindle quotes a dean: "religion... ought to make yer 'appy." Millie asks Bindle to take her to pictures Friday; wear hard hat.

### Ch V Bindle Tries a Change of Work
- Night painting at the Splendid Hotel (dumb painters; no talking; foreman insults). Bindle's paint. Foreman: "Paintin's your job, slippery, not jugglin'." Foreman's silent insult (Brazilian gesture).
- Foreman (Sanders) has beanfeast at Epping; hires Bindle to remove and replace numbers on 1 East corridor doors; offers beer, bread, cheese. Sanders: "If anythin' goes wrong I'll lose my job."
- Chambermaid: "I'm married... A girl would have to have tired arms to rest them round your neck." Bindle's idea.

### Ch VI The Hotel Corridor
- Clergyman (nervous, hair across eye) asks for bathroom; Frenchman with wife in wrong room (No. 24 vs 21). Bindle swaps numbers on doors. Woman in pink neglige finds man in her bed (bald, black whiskers). Young exquisite in silk kimono with girl in his room. Man in monocle vs man in bath-robe over trousers. Deputy-manager; fireman restores numbers with envelopes. Guests reunited.
- Monday: Sanders visits Bindle at home; Mrs. Bindle throws wet dishcloth, hits him with broom, "God forgive me" demanded. Bindle: "Religion... Bank 'Olidays, same as work."

### Ch VII Bindle Commits an Indiscretion
- Bindle at pictures with Millie (Putney Pavilion, not Fulham Grand/Charlie Chaplin film). Millie meets Charlie Dixon (shipping office; Millie typist at wholesale draper's; they met on train). Bindle plays Cupid, leaves them. Millie: "I hate it, Uncle Joe... I want to be happy."
- Hearty bumped by Millie in High Street; Bindle apologises. Millie: "I'm glad you're my uncle." Bindle: "Gawd bless yer, Millikins."
- Charlie asks Bindle's help; Bindle wants letters of respectability. Mrs. Bindle: "Who's the man?"

### Ch VIII The Great Conspiracy
- Harridge's Stores; Barton Bridge Temperance Fete (25th anniversary). Sir John Bilder (Bilder's Entire) supplies ale ("Well, I'm damned!"). Barton Bridge: non-sectarian; Mr. Lacey (nonconformist baker), Mr. Carter (church baker); Lady Knob-Kerrick insisted London caterers (Harridge's).
- Bindle drives pantechnicon; driver. Pack Horse pub; Mr. Cutts (red knitted cap). Dick Little's flask: pure alcohol mixed with distilled mead, poured into Bindle's glass; Bindle: "It ain't for suckin'-babes." Dick Little pays (Bindle refuses sovereign). Dick Little's family: Dr. Little, Tom and Dick.
- Fete preparations; Bindle pours alcohol into casks via stone jars. Vicar Mr. Slocum; Rev. Andrew McFie (Congregational, Auchinlech). Bindle serves spiked lemonade; wild revelry; McFie and Slocum shocked.

### Ch IX The Temperance Fete
- Lady Knob-Kerrick arrives, Miss Isabel Strint; Dick Little bows; she rebuffs ("You may not"). Mr. Marsh (people's churchwarden) chases girl. Morris dancers (Miss Slocum, Miss McFie). Maypole. Mr. Grint (chapel butcher) quadrille. Tool (coachman); Thomas (footman); Saunders (head gardener); Ash (builder).
- Dr. Little: "Is everybody mad?" Vicar drunk ("Make him my curate"). Mr. Wace; McFie sings "Who's your Lady Friend?" McFie (sword-dance in sunbonnet) sprays with fire hose; McFie chases Lady K; hose soaks Lady K and coachman; horses bolt.
- McFie holds meadow with carriage barricade; police (superintendent from Ryford; three cars) hosed. Lady K telephoned Ryford. Fete ends inglorious. Bindle drives off pantechnicon; Dick Little's confession: "pure alcohol mixed with distilled mead."

### Ch X Mr. Hearty Prays for Bindle
- Sunday: Mrs. Bindle reports Hearty prayed for Bindle: "a brother fallen by the wayside, a wheat-ear among thorns." Bindle furious; "Winkles... Gawd."
- Bindle goes to Dick Little's flat, 550 Beaufort Mansions, Beaufort Street. Dick: "Aristophanes." Medical students (Tim's = St. Timothy's Hospital) toast "Bindle the Incomparable." Bindle stands on table; speech; "I'm sick of all this 'umbug."

### Ch XI Mr. Hearty Becomes Extremely Unpopular
- Hearty advertised for dog, housekeeper, errand-boy, adoption of child; Lily (dog, huge mix), owner (ugly, black stumps of teeth); crowds with dogs; vehicles block Fulham High Street; police; Bindle arrives with three pantechnicons. Bindle identifies Hearty as brother-in-law. Crowd sings "Who's your Lady Friend?" Police telephoned; traffic chaos.
- Bindle works late helping Hearty fill orders; Hearty gives Bindle a pineapple.

### Ch XII Bindle Agrees to Become a Millionaire
- Dick Little and Bindle; Tom Little. Reginald Graves ("Gravy"; St. Joseph's College, Oxford; scholarship; grocer father in midland town; invents rich uncle Josiah Williams of Australia; mines and sheep-runs). Graves betrayed Travers's secret (divorce tale) to Dr. Peter.
- Bindle asks £20-30 expenses; agrees to play uncle, "Mr. Josiah Williams."
- *The Oxford Mail* announces Josiah Williams visit ("Mr. Reginald Graves... Bungem's... Sceptre" hotel). Graves gasps.

### Ch XIII Oxford's Welcome to Bindle
- Station: band in scarlet and gold; carriage with four horses (piebald, skewbald, white, pink). Bindle arrives: black-and-white check suit, grey homburg with white puggaree, Ted tie, patent boots, white spats; malacca cane; cigar with red-gold band; star-handkerchief. Cinematograph men, newspaper men (wigs bought from London perruquier).
- Tom Little on Guggers' back. "So you're Polly's boy." Band plays "Auld Lang Syne" and "See the Conquering Hero Comes" muddled. Kangaroo (Horace Trent) on box.
- *Oxford Courier* account: Josiah Williams "had to change my collar."
- Dr. Peter invites Williams to lunch; Graves dreads.
- Bungem's supper (St. Bungem the Hospitable; quatrain by future Poet Laureate "One crowded hour of glorious life / I crave, but let it be with Bungem"). Asparagus à la Bungem; Bindle "Seems as if yer 'ad to 'ave somebody rubbin' yer." Dick Little toasts "Mr. Josiah Williams of Moonagoona... his bleating sheep." Bindle's speech: "Moonaspoona... birth-rate", eels, linnet, beetle, Tom Graves grocer of 60 High Street, Bingley ("sand with sugar", "tea at one-an'-eight"); "Polly"; Graves flees; Bindle's "Leggo my leg!"; men chase Graves; Graves reaches St. Joseph's porter at night.
- Next morning: Tom, Guggers, Travers wake Bindle; "The Master has invited you to lunch"; Bindle returns to London with Dick Little (11.6 train).

### Ch XIV Mr. Hearty Gives a Party
- Hearty's party (Friday) for Sopley, Winch (missionary, Alton Road Chapel), Heartys' guests, Flinders (grocer; wife). Mrs. Hearty insists Bindle invited. Mrs. Bindle's dress (black alpaca, green satin yoke) and bonnet; Bindle in dress-suit (red silk handkerchief, diamond stud). Mrs. Bindle: "Where'd you get that dress-suit?" Bindle: "I 'ad it give to me..."
- Party: oranges, bananas, pineapple (uncut), lemonade; "Looping, Looping" game; Mr. Flinders forced to sing "Queen of the Earth"; Tibbins (Persian kitten). Winch with Bindle; "Blind Man's Buff" (Bindle identifies Sopley by whiskers, mistaking him for Millie). Sopley's beard; "Follow my Leader".
- Bindle's vote-of-thanks speech; Mr. Hearty "Thank you, Joseph, for—"; Mrs. Bindle hears Sopley's invitation to Bazaar.

### Ch XV Bindle and the German Menace
- Bindle and Ginger (foreman Brooks) at Holmleigh, Little Compton (Suffolk) moving Mr. Henry Miller's firearms collection (Lowestoft quarters). Mr. Gandy (Dove and Easel; velvet skullcap; Dundreary whiskers) talks; Bindle hints "the fort." Bindle collects half-crown/ five shillings from Mrs. Grinder and Mr. Greenhales (tells them of "the fort").
- Sir Charles Custance (magistrate; "invasion"; Dorcas Society complaint). Sergeant Wrannock (Suffolk Constabulary). Sir Charles visits Holmleigh; met by Mr. Gandy (insulted). Foreman dismisses Sir Charles ("Hi, Ginger?"). Mr. Greenhales (Holmleigh; false teeth; wig) visits; foreman sends him off. Sergeant Wrannock with bicycle; foreman calls him "cockie." Sir Charles and Wrannock plan to meet at The Towers at six.

### Ch XVI The Amateur Detectives
- Bindle and foreman on night duty at Holmleigh. Foreman (Brooks) takes watch; Bindle slips away. Sir Charles, Greenhales, Gandy, Wrannock sneak in; Gandy through scullery window; Greenhales through dining-room window; Wrannock to scullery? (all captured). Foreman drops them in the empty pantechnicon, barred and padlocked: Wrannock, Greenhales, Gandy, Sir Charles (bled from head). Mr. Richard Miller (new tenant, tall, thin, 38-40).
- Inspector from Lowestoft and plain-clothes men. Foreman reports "the band"; Miller: "I am supposed to have the finest collection of firearms in the country." Bindle vanishes: "Funny none of 'em seem to see the joke!"

### Ch XVII Bindle Makes a Mistake
- Manager of West London Furniture Depository, Ltd. Sir Charles's letter (complaint against Bindle and foreman). Bindle offers to resign and rejoin later. Bindle sent to move Mrs. Rogers's furniture from 181 Branksome Road (West Kensington) to 33 Lebanon Avenue, Chiswick (Granger) — but key given was 131 (sergeant's error). Vans No. 6 and No. 8; crew Wilkes, Huggles, Randers, new man, Ginger. Bindle moves Mr. Rogers's Branksome Road furniture (No. 131) to Lebanon Avenue; "Mrs. Rogers" at No. 129 complains.
- Railton-Rogers (bald, Thames-tug fussy; "What's that?"; wife Emily "sleeping partner"; seven children incl. Eustace, Nelly, Muriel) arrive; find house empty; police; Mrs. Clark (neighbour; complains of Bindle's insolence); Archie Clark (12) on bicycle identifies Chiswick address.
- Granger (burly, blue eyes) and wife (porcelain smile) at Lebanon Avenue; Rogers attacks; policeman takes all to station. Bindle dismissed Monday: "Lorst yer job?" "Yes... but it was worth it."

### Ch XVIII Bindle Assists in an Elopement
- Bindle tries to enlist (Kitchener's Army); doctor: varicose veins; "couldn't stand the marching." Bindle sworn in as special constable at local police-station (equipment: truncheon, armlet, whistle). Tells Hearty.
- Night on Putney Hill: Dick Little (Ethel Knob-Kerrick, Lady K's daughter, brunette, tilted chin). Plan: Guggers' Rolls-Royce; ladder; Ethel over garden wall; Miss Strint. Lady K finds ladder, falls on Strint ("Help! Help!!").
- Bindle captured; before Lady K, Thomas and Wilton; Bindle's "uniform." Inspector arrives; Lady K pays £5 (five one-pound notes) to Bindle. Dick and Ethel escape to Walton (Guggers' sister).

### Ch XIX The Scarlet Horse Coterie
- Friday nights at The Scarlet Horse (small room). Visitors: Ginger (Chiswick), Huggles (West Kensington), Wilkes (Hammersmith), Ruddy Bill, Tom Cave, Weary, Ted, "Whiskers", Charlie.
- Ruddy Bill's obscenities; Bindle corrects him. Ginger enlisted after "that rosy song" (Gospel/ rosy song). Bindle on war: Germany's "place in the sun"; "arbitration"; "Gawd strike me dead if I won't." Bindle's marriage tale (mate with top hat).

### Ch XX Millie Leaves Home
- Millie's happiness; Hearty notices. Bindle takes Millie to pictures; leaves cinema; Hearty met them and took Millie home. Charlie waits at cinema. Bindle and Charlie confront Hearty; Hearty demands explanation; forbids Millie to see Charlie. Millie: "I wish he was my father." Millie leaves with Bindle. Bindle to Charlie: "Next time you're grateful... put it down on paper."
- Mrs. Bindle takes Millie upstairs; Bindle promises chapel on Sunday; Mrs. Bindle sobs. Bindle: "Funny things, women."

### Ch XXI Conclusion
- Two weeks later at Dick Little's flat (Chelsea Palace Mansions). Millie engaged; Charlie enlisted; Hearty changed. Mrs. Bindle gives pickles. Dick Little and Ettie (Mrs. Little) married. Bindle: "Got a job?"; "It can't be all 'oney livin' with an 'eathen such as me." Ettie: "a perfect dear." Dick Little's Theodore Hook joke (the dog/housekeeper prank Bindle suspects Dick did). END.

**Backmatter:** Other Herbert Jenkins titles listed (The Bindles on the Rocks, Bindle, The Night Club, John Dene of Toronto, Malcolm Sage Detective, Mrs. Bindle, Patricia Brent Spinster, The Rain Girl, The Return of Alfred, The Stiffsons; Herbert Jenkins' Splendid Library titles).
